answers.assumption_check: Load-bearing: (1) a real caller of a deleted thing has a proof that runs it, so running the namers' proofs measures callers; a namer with no proof is reported as unmeasured, never assumed safe; (2) bin/cairn test <proofs...> runs each proof under the tester's seal and prints one '  green|red  <path>' line per proof; (3) moving the targets into a temp folder and moving them back on red restores them byte for byte, tracked or not; (4) the command does not commit: the caller commits by path.
answers.builder_check: A Haiku builder needs: (1) namers = repo files (walk, skip dot-dirs, __pycache__, *.egg-info, validations/, history.json, state.json, verdict-*.json, the targets) whose text holds a target's repo path or, for a .py or a folder under cairn/ or skills/, its dotted module; (2) proofs to run = namers matching */proofs/test_*.py, plus for a code namer (.py, .sh, or an executable under a bin/) every proofs/test_*.py of the nearest ancestor holding intention+why.json; a namer with neither is listed as unmeasured; (3) runner(repo, proofs) -> {path: 'green'|'red'}, default runs bin/cairn test and parses '^\s+(green|red)\s+(\S+)$'; (4) exit 0 retired, 1 restored, 2 usage; (5) shortcut cairn/devices/codemother/bin/retire copies bin/outline's sys.path shape.
